headline:
Planning took 375.9 min because Luna wrote about 1.15 million output tokens (59% hidden reasoning) at a near-constant 55 tokens/s [M]. A model request was in flight 99.3% of the window; every ShipLoop command together ran about 10 s there (22 s over the whole run). The scripts are not the cost. The protocol they prescribe is: Improve review children 203 min (54%), the plan stage's Backchain work 64 (17%), all other authoring 108 (29%). Retries, refusals, compaction and kill recovery together are at most about 90 min [I, upper bound]; removing all of it still leaves 285 or more. Release 1.21.0's one-pass Backchain default cut the OLD window from 648 to 376 min; Improve did not shrink and is now the largest block.

Sonnet's 4.7 min is not like-for-like: no Backchain, review notes of about 270 bytes, 9 KB of planning docs.

A 7-minute window is at most about 23k output tokens. The final planning docs (116 KB) are that size written once with no thinking. Seven minutes is not reachable on Luna with this design [I]. It needs a different one: about 20-25 KB of planning text, no model-run Improve or Backchain loop in the window, roughly one turn per stage. That conflicts with S-10, enterprise rigour and S-11.

The ledgers cannot say what the 683k reasoning tokens contain, what dropping review would cost downstream (both runs had a 123-166 min replan that review missed), or why the LIVE run stopped mid-response at 14:32Z.

what_is_going_on:
Mechanism [M unless marked]. Wall time is output tokens divided by a nearly constant decode rate, plus a fixed cost per response. Planning emitted 1,153,899 output tokens in 757 responses in 375.9 min: 3,069 tokens per wall minute (OLD 3,078). Regression of response time on output tokens (F/verify_out.txt sec 2): 17.99 s per 1k tokens plus 2.18 s per response, R2 0.993, i.e. 55.6 tok/s marginal; total output including reasoning predicts time, visible tokens alone do not (R2 0.43). So decode explains 345.9 min (92.0%) and per-response latency 27.5 min (7.3%); together 99.3%, the in-flight share. Compaction (3.1%) is inside both, not an extra. Tool wait is about 0.9 min.

Where the tokens go (A3, planning window). Reasoning 682.6k (59.2%; encrypted, content unreadable). It is concentrated: median 347 reasoning tokens per response, p90 2,415, max 18,987; 189 responses with 1,000 or more hold 519k (76%). 629 of 757 responses emit under 1,000 visible tokens yet carry 60.5% of all output tokens and 231.6 min. Visible 471.3k: planning-doc writes 82.3k (7.1% of output), other file writes 142.5k (Backchain artifacts, Improve review records, notes, scratch), ad-hoc check scripts 50.6k, short commands and narration 58.7k, per-call plumbing 100.4k, compaction summaries 37.1k. File-write payload in the window was 912.7k characters, planning docs 39% of it. Docs were rewritten about 3.1x (A3: 355k chars emitted vs 116k final); git agrees in direction: spec first commit 20,590 B vs 24,135 final, test-strategy 20,968 vs 28,780, plan 20,328 vs 25,583, test-spec 18,020 vs 22,339, i.e. first versions are 73-85% of final size. Time by activity (A3): writing planning docs 75.3 min (20.1%), ad-hoc check scripts 73.8 (19.7%), reads of references, docs and packets 91.0 (24.3%).

Why Improve is half the window. 5 children, 22 passes (spec 5, test-strategy 8, plan 4, step-plan 4, test-spec 1): 12 changed something (146.5 min), 10 changed nothing (28.2 min); 9 of those 10 are the gate's terminal confirmations (25.7 min). Pass 1 is a second authoring pass: it changed files in 4 of 5 children (74.4 min). Opening each child cost 1.2-10.5 min (26.3 in total). Each child carries about 247 KB of review paperwork vs 112 KB of reviewed docs [A7]; review-N text alone is 84.9 KB over the 22 planning passes (3.9 KB per pass). Pass labels (warranted 5, minor 5, correction of an earlier pass 2, no change 10) are my judgement [I]. The longest pass of the replan, step-plan #2 pass 2 (37.1 min, 112.9k tokens of which 73.8k reasoning, no repo file changed), found one material item: the result summary claimed a source-aware check still complete although it was bound to the earlier candidate hash; it corrected the wording and the decision note [M, run/.../reviews/review-2.md].

The Backchain stage. The plan packet runs a one-pass Backchain loop (default in 1.21.0). Its 64.1 min are 22.5 min of reading and the first plan.md draft before any Backchain artifact, 15.2 min building the candidate and checking it, 21.8 min Until Loop pass, 4.6 min result. OLD's loops at plan and step-plan took 322.5 min of phase wall (7 plus 4 passes). Nothing else shrank.

Context churn amplifies. The window is 258,400 tokens; compaction fires at 240-256k input, every 32.6 min on average (about 63 responses). Tool output returned to the model in planning is about 7.0M chars, more than the model emitted; 96 calls hit the 40 KB host cap [A6]. 180 of 1,115 tool outputs (16%) carry a host truncation marker, 1,364,869 tokens cut in all. Each of the 4 resumed sessions read the 68 KB ShipLoop SKILL.md and received 40.1k chars (one 32.2k) with the middle cut; only those 4 reads of that file exist in the run (F/verify_out.txt sec 4; rollouts). After a compaction the first productive call comes a mean 195 s later [A5]; 50% of doc-read calls fall within 10 min after one [A6].

Redundancy [I]. The same facts are restated in every document (F-TEST appears 9-10 times in each of spec, strategy, plan, test-spec; randomUUID in four documents and three work items) [A6]. Docs paraphrase each other, so size multiplies.

Design defect outside the window. The test-red revise at 11:20:39Z (the focused suite imports ../game.js, which no step created) re-ran step-plan with a Backchain loop and a 4-pass Improve, 3.1x the first step-plan (120.1 vs 38.7 min), 165.9 min with the stages that followed. OLD's analogue was an implement revise costing 123.4 min. No planning-stage review pass in either run raised it (n=2, one request, both with review on).

What is NOT the cause. ShipLoop script execution (about 10 s in the window). Tool execution (0.2%). LIVE API stalls (none over 120 s unexplained; OLD lost 17.7 min, 1.5%, to a 12-min stderr-confirmed outage and a 5.8-min unexplained stall). Retries and refusals (3.8% central, 8.9% ceiling). Interruptions (at most 14.8%). The 'killed three times' premise (four). The sub-agent in OLD (overlapped, not added).

How to read the lever list. Savings are alternatives against the same minutes (Improve windows 203.4 contain the open step, the confirmation passes and the check scripts; the authoring-size lever overlaps all of them). Sum none of them without re-basing. Stage times vary about 2x run to run (prior design-final.json caveat), each cell here is n=1.
seven_minute_math:
BUDGET [M rate, I arithmetic]. Marginal decode 55.6 tok/s (OLS, F/verify_out.txt; A1 54.4, A2 55.5, A3 54.87, A7 55.6) plus 2.18 s per response. 420 s allows at most 23.4k output tokens including reasoning if the model never stops decoding. The planning protocol has at least 10 stage acceptances; at 30 responses (3 per stage, assumed) latency alone takes 65 s, leaving about 19.7k tokens. At LIVE's reasoning share (59-61%) only 8-9.6k are visible, 32-38 KB at about 4 characters per token, before per-call plumbing (about 132 tokens per response, A3). Realistic planning text is therefore about 20-25 KB [I]; 36-40 KB is the ceiling with one response and no overhead. At the window's mean 1,524 tokens per response (29.6 s) 7 minutes holds about 14 responses.

WHAT PLANNING PRODUCES against 23.4k (LIVE window): output 1,153,899 = 49x; reasoning 682,569 = 29x; visible 471,330 = 20x; planning-doc writes including rewrites about 84k tokens = 3.6x; the final docs written once, 116,148 B = 27.5-31.4k tokens = 1.2-1.3x the whole budget = 8.3-9.4 min of pure decode with no thinking and no latency; the four core docs (spec 24,135 + test-strategy 28,780 + plan 25,583 + test-spec 22,339 = 100,837 B, 23.8-27k tokens) = 7.1-8.1 min, the entire budget. OLD window: 1,995k tokens = 85x.

WHAT CANNOT FIT, whatever the content. Any Improve child (shortest LIVE bind-to-accept 12.1 min; opening 1.2-10.5 min; a clean confirmation pass 1.4-3.8 min and the gate needs two in a row after a change). Any Backchain loop (the one Until Loop pass was 21.8 min, 08:00:41-08:22:31Z). A resume (orientation to first advance 1.1-18.2 min per kill [A2]). At LIVE sizes pure decode of one write: spec 1.8 min, test-strategy 2.2, plan 1.9, test-spec 1.7, decisions 0.5, environment 0.3.
 Floor with no model-run Improve and no Backchain loop beyond the plan.md first draft: 108.5 (other authoring) + 7 to 22.5 (plan.md draft with or without the reading that precedes it) = 115-131 min, 17-19x the target [M timestamps, I for what the plan stage would do without Backchain]. The draft's 149.7 min 'no review, no Backchain' floor (A7) was not a floor: it still contained 37.6 min of Backchain preparation and 4.6 of result. Scaling by Sonnet's 12x smaller documents (about 12 min) is rejected as an estimate: intake, discovery, research, prepare and select-work took 131k output tokens (41.5 min) to produce about 5.5k tokens of final text (A3), so their cost is reasoning and reading, not document size.

WHAT SONNET DOES DIFFERENTLY (re-checked, F/verify_out.txt sec 9; run e2e-runs/20261003/batch-sonnet/battleship, plugin 1.16.0). Planning window 4.73 min (4.83 from the first event) over 10 actions. It ran no Backchain: no backchain file exists under .shiploop-runs; the prior team report says the same for every Sonnet run and that Luna's Improve pass costs 8.8 min against Sonnet's 0.23 (38x) while documents differ 10-40x. Its 5 planning Improve children took 13 passes in 125 s (about 4 s per pass); its review notes total 6,564 B over 24 passes (about 270 B per pass) against Luna LIVE's 84,886 B over 22 planning passes (3.9 KB per pass), 14x per pass. Planning docs total about 9.3 KB (spec 1,982 B, test-strategy 3,512, plan 784, test-spec 2,281, environment 476) vs 116 KB. In the window it made 45 distinct messages with 83 content events: 870 chars of text and 57,468 chars of tool-input JSON, about 14-16k visible tokens [I from M chars]. Its thinking blocks are empty in the stream, so its reasoning is unmeasurable, and metrics.json's 10,517 output tokens is an undercount. So the data point shows that token volume decides; it does not show that document size is the cause, and it is not the same loop shape.
 Replay check [I]: the same 14-16k visible tokens and 45 responses on Luna would cost 4.2-4.8 min decode plus 1.6 min latency = 5.8-6.4 min at zero reasoning, and about 12-13 min at Luna's 59% reasoning share. Even Sonnet's near-empty planning would not meet 7 minutes on Luna unless reasoning fell to about a third of output.

VERDICT. With the current design on Luna 7 minutes is not reachable. Reaching it needs, at once: about 20-25 KB of planning text, no model-run Improve or Backchain loop in the window, about one turn per stage, per-item W1 planning outside the window (96.0 min), and no compaction or resume inside it. That is a different design, not a tuning, and no run has tried it, so its quality cost is unmeasured.

levers.lever: No model-run Improve at the planning stages (spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec). Replace with script-run checks plus one review after the first RED or at the end.
levers.saves: Gross 203.4 min (54.1% of the window), window 172.5 min [M timestamps]. Also removes about 247 KB of review paperwork and the opening cost (26.3). Net is lower: pass 1 is a second authoring pass (74.4 min, first drafts are 73-85% of final size), so part of it moves to the producer (unmeasured share). All lever savings are alternatives against the same minutes; sum none of them without re-basing.
levers.cost_or_risk: Forgoes 5 warranted fixes, 5 minor and 2 corrections in the window (traceability, fixture bypass of the real rules module, /api/new recovery untested, JSON content-type oracles, W3 ready-check). Break-even against an escaped defect: the replan chain cost 120-166 min (LIVE 165.9, OLD 123.4), so the saving is saving minus p x (120-166) with p the unmeasured escape rate; one extra escape per run erases most or all of it. Observed: both replan defects escaped with review on (n=2, one request), which says nothing about the rate with review off.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Steps iterate until a check confirms each exit criterion (primary); S-10 (loops iterate until their exit condition); enterprise rigour even for small requests. Supports S-9 only if the replacement check is script-run.

levers.lever: Improve single pass at planning stages: keep open, pass 1 and close, drop passes 2..N. This is an engine change, not a flag.
levers.saves: Gross 100.3 min (26.8%); about 89.5 net of the K1 kill orientation that sits inside a later pass; window about 275-286 [M/I]. Needs: the contract literal required_trivial_reviews=2 (shiploop_navigator.py line 4070), the import validator (shiploop_standalone_improve.py lines 617-621, 'does not meet Improve's two-review minimum'; it also requires the last report trivial), their tests, and an S-10 amendment (the existing carve-out covers the Backchain child only). The earlier 'runtime already supports it' reading was wrong: only the vendored Until Loop supports gate 0.
levers.cost_or_risk: Gives up 2 of 5 warranted fixes (both test-strategy), 4 minor, 2 corrections; later passes cost about 45 min per fix vs about 20 for pass 1 (kill-adjusted). Pass 1 stays a second authoring pass. Carries one-supported-version and spec-admission costs. Same escaped-defect break-even as L1.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: S-10 (no iteration cap except the stated carve-out); the owner's rule that loops are unbounded; iterate until a check confirms the exit criterion.

levers.lever: One Improve review over all planning docs at the end of planning instead of one child per document.
levers.saves: 118-178 min [A7, I], window 257-197. Removes four of five opening costs and four sets of paperwork. Not additive with L1 or L2.
levers.cost_or_risk: Defects found after downstream docs were written against them; pass-1 authoring-style work is conserved so the conservative figure applies. Cascade cost unmeasured. Same escaped-defect break-even.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Iterate-until-confirmed per stage; S-11 if per-stage knowledge is committed at each close.

levers.lever: Gate needs one clean review instead of two (engine change, same files as L2).
levers.cost_or_risk: Small gain; the second confirmation is the only evidence of a no-change state. Not worth it on its own.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Two consecutive no-change passes is the stated stop rule; S-10.

levers.lever: Script-enforced size caps on planning artifacts: per-document and total (about 20-25 KB total fits a 7-minute window at today's reasoning share); lint refuses oversize.
levers.saves: Direct authoring only: 'write planning docs' is 75.3 min, so a cap at 40 KB saves about 49 min [I, 75.3 x (1-40/116)]. Whether review, rewrite and read cost scale with size is unmeasured: no run varies size at a fixed model and loop shape, and Sonnet is not evidence (see F12). No larger figure is supported.
levers.cost_or_risk: Oracle specificity is consumed downstream (19 of 21 test-spec literals appear in tests), so a hard cap may drop content test-author needs; refusals add retries; the cap needs a split rule for what goes to the retained knowledge store.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Verbose prompts over size bounds (raise the bound, don't trim) and 'packets point to files, never trim guidance'; enterprise rigour; S-11. KISS and 'prompts: concise, meaningful change' support it.

levers.lever: Merge or skip stages for small requests: fold intake, discovery and research into one authoring turn; skip prepare and select-work when there is a single work item.
levers.saves: intake 3.4 + discovery 10.6 + research 10.1 + prepare 14.7 + select-work 2.7 = 41.5 min if all dropped; realistically 20-30 [I].
levers.cost_or_risk: decisions.md and environment.md are consumed by later planning stages (read by 12 and 16 stage instances) and are the retained knowledge; merging may lower their quality. The test-spec Improve child changed nothing on both LIVE visits (7.5 and 7.4 min), but that is one run: OLD's test-spec children changed things (5 passes 54.5 min, W2 M1 T2; second visit 8 passes 45.3 min, W1 M2 C1 T4; labels are my judgement), so dropping that review is not established. test-spec itself is heavily consumed (7 delivery stages).
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: S-11 (planning knowledge retained); enterprise rigour. KISS supports.

levers.lever: Lazy per-item planning: close the planning window at plan acceptance and treat W1 select-work, step-plan and test-spec as delivery.
levers.saves: 96.0 min leave the window (375.9 to 279.9) [A1] but not the run: wall to green is unchanged. A real saving only if step-plan is derived from the first failing test instead of reviewed before RED; both runs' pre-RED step plans needed a replan (LIVE 145.3, OLD 95.9 min).
levers.cost_or_risk: Relabels time unless step-plan is actually removed; deriving the step plan after RED changes the stage graph and the test-red contract.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: S-9 is aligned; enterprise rigour (planned steps before code) is strained.

levers.lever: Planning budget enforced by the script: a wall-time budget per stage (timeline stamps exist), escalating to close or split when exceeded.
levers.saves: Bounds the tail by construction, but at today's document sizes a 7-min budget cannot be met (final docs alone are 8.3-9.4 min of decode); it would force early close with partial docs unless L1, L5 and L13 come first.
levers.cost_or_risk: Token counts are not visible to a host-neutral script; time budgets truncate real work; interacts badly with kills and compactions (12-43 min of loss per kill).
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Directly strains the owner's rule that ShipLoop loops are unbounded (no cap, no revise/blocked for running long) and S-14 (unattended default). Needs an explicit carve-out for planning.

levers.lever: Effort per stage: lower reasoning effort for read, navigation and check turns; keep high for review and authoring.
levers.saves: Unknown; no experiment prices it. Reasoning is 682.6k planning tokens (about 207.6 min) and 76% of it sits in 189 responses with 1,000 or more reasoning tokens, so a per-stage knob has something to act on, but the only measured contrast (max to xhigh, same-graph stages) moved tokens -4% and time -8% with per-response size up 35% and reasoning share unchanged (61.9% vs 61.6%), confounded with the version change. Effort below xhigh was never run. The draft's 57 min was a hypothesis and is withdrawn.
levers.cost_or_risk: Quality effect unmeasured; may raise typo and refusal rates; host-dependent whether a skill can set effort per stage.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Luna pin (every Luna call at max, E2E at xhigh); enterprise rigour.

levers.lever: Cached stack and skill references plus a retained knowledge digest, so each stage and each resume does not re-read ShipLoop SKILL.md (68 KB, read 4x), Improve references and the planning docs.
levers.saves: Reads of guidance 34.5-42.3 min (9-11% of window) plus compaction (11.6 call + 17.5-20.0 recovery). Avoiding a third to a half: about 15-35 min [I]. Plan#1 alone read 67 guidance files (851 KB) [A6].
levers.cost_or_risk: Stale digest; the model still re-reads documents it must edit; cache design work.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Aligned with S-11, 'reference, not reread' and the cached-stack-references TODO; low tension.

levers.lever: Script-owned deterministic document checks (extend shiploop lint: links, anchors, ID traceability, whitespace, identity hashes) instead of model-authored check scripts.
levers.saves: Ad-hoc check scripts are 121 responses, 73.8 min (19.7% of window), 100 scripts, at least 20 hand-written link/anchor checkers [A3]. Half to three quarters plausible: about 35-55 min [I]. Overlaps L1 (some of these run inside Improve passes). Also removes the SyntaxError retries (5 in the window).
levers.cost_or_risk: Some scripts are real content checks the lint cannot express; lint must be fast and never refuse for style.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Aligned with S-9 and 'scripts own graph navigation'; low tension.

levers.lever: Shrink Improve protocol overhead: generate checks.md and opening.md from the real check run, cut the replacement handoff, shorten the open step.
levers.saves: Open step 26.3 min (7.0% of window); paperwork about 247 KB, at least 20 min of decode [A7]. Estimate 26-46 min [I]. Lies inside L1's 203.4 min.
levers.cost_or_risk: The evidence records are what the script verifies; trimming them weakens the audit trail.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Iterate-until-confirmed needs evidence; 'prompts: concise, meaningful change' supports trimming ineffective detail.

levers.lever: Set --backchain-passes none (shipped in 1.21.0, no code change; modes one|converge|none, default one). Keep the script's structural backchain-check.
levers.saves: 22 min (the one Until Loop pass, 21.8) to about 57 (64.1 minus the roughly 7-min plan.md first draft) [I]; the replan's Backchain loop 41.2 on top. The upper figure assumes the plan stage is satisfied by plan.md alone without the Backchain reading block (the CHANGELOG says none omits the six-file resource block and requests no whole plan/draft); what the model then does at the plan stage was not verified. The draft's 40.5-63.5 min double-counted the plan.md draft.
levers.cost_or_risk: The graph had no delivery reader in either run [A6], but its structural check found a real fault at the replan (duplicated seam confirmation, 3 needs without source facts) [A7]; ownership and trace value is not measured in minutes. Audit stages still run one Backchain pass after a finding.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Backchain is for ownership and trace, not minutes; S-10 carve-out already relaxes this loop to one pass; enterprise rigour.

levers.lever: Mechanical retry fixes: print the working directory and exact next/done lines in the packet head, mkdir run/notes at init, drop derivable flags, have refusals name the keys found.
levers.saves: Up to 14.2 min planning (19.6 whole run) [A4], about 4% of the window. Typos are repaired by the next call in 28 of 61 cases (median 11-14 s).
levers.cost_or_risk: Low; does not move the number toward 7 min.

levers.lever: Harness-only: avoid the 2-hour background-task kills (foreground or longer limit) and make the resume prompt carry the exact run-dir path and pass state.
levers.saves: 1.3 dead + 10-23 orientation in the planning window, up to about 43 by pass-length excess [A5]; 2 of LIVE's path typos came within 17 s of a resume.
levers.cost_or_risk: Not a product lever; the LIVE run stopped at 14:32Z for an unknown reason before its next limit.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: None; the stored 'tasks die at about 30 min' note is stale (the kill interval measured 120.3 min).

levers.lever: Model per planning stage: a faster or cheaper model for intake, discovery, research and script-call turns, Luna for authoring.
levers.saves: Unpriced. Those stages took 3.4 + 10.6 + 10.1 + 14.7 + 2.7 = 41.5 min of Luna and 131k output tokens. The only data point for another model is Sonnet's 4.83-min window (about 14-16k visible tokens), which did far less work, so it bounds nothing. Quality unmeasured.
levers.cost_or_risk: Mixed-model handoff cost and consistency; E2E validity changes.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Luna pin (every Luna call at max, E2E at xhigh); experiments-use rules.

levers.lever: Make the revise path cheaper: a test-red revise should not re-run a full Backchain loop plus a 4-pass Improve on the whole step-plan.
levers.saves: Up to 66.7 min per escape (165.9 vs 99.2 min for the redone stages) [M cost, I saving]; the replan step-plan alone cost 3.1x the first (120.1 vs 38.7). It lowers the price of every escape, so it makes L1-L3 safer.
levers.cost_or_risk: CHANGELOG says a repair/revise after a finding still runs one Backchain pass by design; trimming it trades trace for minutes.

levers.lever: Keep skill and reference reads under the host's output cap (or print them in chunks), so a resumed session never receives a SKILL.md with its middle cut.
levers.saves: At most 13.6 min in the planning window (17.2 whole run) by a heuristic upper bound [I]; cost of the cut itself is unmeasured.
levers.cost_or_risk: Low; chunking adds calls. Needs a test of whether a resumed session works from a truncated SKILL.md first.
levers.owner_rule_in_tension: Aligned with 'reference, not reread' and 'packets point to files'; low tension.

REJECTED: the draft's L9 saving of about 57 min (hypothetical, no experiment) and its 'xhigh vs max gave nothing visible' as a conclusion; replaced by 'unknown' with the measured contrast (-4% tokens, -8% time, +35% per-response size, confounded).

REJECTED: the draft's 12x-linear estimate 'Sonnet's 12x smaller documents put the no-review floor near 12 min', its 149.7-min 'no review, no Backchain' floor, and the Sonnet 'because' / 'same loop shape' claims (Attack 2 findings 1 and 6, Attack 1 finding 2).
